reading.title: What Started the Fire?
reading.intro_zh: 本文讲真实世界里调查人员如何判定野火的起因——这正是 Lesson 53“查原因、排除可能、还原因果”的现实版。内容改编自美国土地管理局（Bureau of Land Management）2024 年发布的野火调查权威科普文章。

source.title: How to Investigate a Wildland Fire

passage: When a wildfire has finally been brought under control, the demanding work of investigation has only just begun. Determining how a blaze ignited is rarely straightforward, because the very flames that swept across the landscape also consumed much of the evidence. Specialists known as fire investigators must think like detectives, tracing the destruction backwards to a single point. Scorched vegetation often burns outward in a distinctive V-shaped pattern, and the narrow tip of that V marks the area of origin. By reading subtle indicators in the char angles and burn marks left on surviving vegetation, investigators can deduce the direction from which the flames advanced and, eventually, the precise spot where the fire began.

Pinpointing the origin is only half the puzzle; the cause must still be established. Investigators draw a sharp distinction between natural and human ignition. Some fires are started naturally, by lightning storms. Far more often, however, the source turns out to be human activity. According to the Bureau of Land Management, roughly 85 percent of wildfires reported nationally each year are human-caused.

Certain causes appear time and again in investigation records: escaped campfires, the burning of debris, equipment failures such as wheel bearing malfunctions, target shooting, powerline faults, and deliberate arson. Working systematically through the evidence, investigators apply the scientific method — gathering data, forming hypotheses, and eliminating alternatives one by one until a credible explanation remains. That knowledge is far from merely academic: it allows land management agencies to design targeted prevention programmes that may spare forests, communities, and lives in the years ahead.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Lightning is responsible for the majority of wildfires worldwide.
Firefighters are usually unable to put out large wildfires.
Investigators use careful methods to find where and why a wildfire started.
Wildfires destroy so much evidence that their causes can never be known.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕调查人员如何先找到火源点（origin），再判定起因（cause），所以主旨是“调查人员用细致的方法查清野火发生的地点和原因”。

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the narrow tip of the V-shaped burn pattern indicate?
options: The area where the fire began.
The direction in which the wind was blowing.
The place where firefighters first arrived.
The total area the fire eventually destroyed.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说 the narrow tip of that V marks the area of origin，即 V 形烧痕的窄端标示着起火点。

questions.question: Which of the following sets of wildfire causes is mentioned in the passage?
options: Farming, mining, construction, and deforestation.
Smoking in forests, illegal hunting, logging, and camping.
Flooding, high winds, prolonged drought, and extreme heat.
Escaped campfires, debris burning, equipment failures, and arson.
questions.explanation_zh: 第三段明确列举了 escaped campfires、burning of debris、equipment failures（如车轮轴承故障）以及 arson（纵火）作为野火的常见人为成因。

questions.question: What can be inferred about why investigators identify the cause of a wildfire?
options: So that the people responsible can always be punished in court.
So that agencies can develop strategies to prevent future fires.
So that the destroyed forest can be rebuilt more quickly.
So that lightning can be removed as a natural threat.
questions.explanation_zh: 结尾说查清原因后 it allows land management agencies to design targeted prevention programmes，可推断查因是为了帮助机构制定预防未来火灾的策略。

questions.question: In the second paragraph, the phrase “roughly 85 percent of wildfires … are human-caused” suggests that human activity is:
options: the dominant source of wildfires in the United States.
reported mainly by people who witness fires starting.
more dangerous to people than to forests.
unrelated to the way investigators work.
questions.explanation_zh: 85% 这一数字直接说明人类活动是野火的主要（dominant）来源，即 human activity is the dominant source of wildfires in the United States。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 53 的五个“调查原因”句式升级到 B2+：用 At last 写漫长努力终于有结果，用 Since then...have been trying to... 写持续不断的探究，用 are often caused by... 写抽象原因归因，用 were not able to find... 写证据缺失，最后用 In this way...solved the mystery 写凭借推理解开谜团。

patterns.title: At last, ...
patterns.source: At last firemen have put out a big forest fire.
patterns.focus_zh: At last 放在句首，表示一件拖了很久、让人着急的事终于有了结果。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一项耗时漫长、令人焦灼的研究、调查或谈判终于取得了决定性的突破。
patterns.sample: At last, after months of painstaking analysis, the investigators identified the overlooked detail that finally explained the accident.
patterns.tip_zh: At last 后面通常接一个完整句子，语气是“终于”。

patterns.title: Since then, ... have been trying to ...
patterns.source: Since then, they have been trying to find out how the fire began.
patterns.focus_zh: Since then 指“从那以后”；have been trying to 强调这件事一直在持续努力。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写自某个关键时刻以来，一个团队一直在持续不懈地探究某个复杂或抽象的问题。
patterns.sample: Since then, scientists across several institutions have been trying to determine why the once-stable ecosystem has begun to collapse so rapidly.
patterns.tip_zh: 主语用 we/they 时，后面自然接 have been trying to；再接动词原形。

patterns.title: are often caused by ...
patterns.source: Forest fires are often caused by broken glass or by cigarette ends.
patterns.focus_zh: are often caused by 用来写“某种结果通常由什么原因造成”，很适合解释常见原因。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一种社会现象或系统性问题通常由哪些深层原因造成。
patterns.sample: Devastating wildfires are often caused by prolonged drought, careless human activity, and the gradual accumulation of dry vegetation.
patterns.tip_zh: 先写结果，再用 are often caused by 接两个可能原因。

patterns.title: were not able to find ...
patterns.source: They were not able to find any broken glass.
patterns.focus_zh: were not able to find 比 did not find 更突出“努力找过，但没有找到”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写研究人员经过反复细致的检查后，仍无法找到他们原本预期会出现的关键证据。
patterns.sample: Despite searching the scorched ground for hours, the investigators were not able to find any trace of the suspected ignition source.
patterns.tip_zh: 后面可以接 any evidence, any marks, any water，让“没有证据”更清楚。

patterns.title: In this way, ... solved the mystery
patterns.source: In this way, he was able to solve the mystery.
patterns.focus_zh: In this way 用来回指前面的方法或线索，再说明谜题被解开。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人凭借一条不起眼的线索或一连串严密的推理，最终揭开了一个长期困扰众人的谜团。
patterns.sample: In this way, by patiently piecing together fragments of charred evidence, the analyst finally unraveled the mystery that had baffled everyone.
patterns.tip_zh: 先想清楚“this way”指哪一步，再写 solved the mystery，句子会更有逻辑。
